question.problem:
For $x,y,z\in {R}^{2},$ consider the following functions: 

$$
\begin{aligned} & y(x)=Ax\,\text{where}\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & z(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}^{2} \\ {y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & f(z)=Cz\,\text{where}\,C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & 2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=A{x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}2(1) & 0 \\ 0 & 2(3)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x))){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}{|}_{{z}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & 6 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}28 & 44 \\ 18 & 24\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Using the chain rule, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))=dfdz⋅dzdy⋅dydx.

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

  • The function f acts on a vector z∈R2 by multiplying it by C and outputs a vector f(z)∈R2. Thus, dfdz=C.

  • The function z acts on a vector y∈R2 and outputs a vector z(y)∈R2. Thus, dzdy=[∂z1∂y1∂z1∂y2∂z2∂y1∂z2∂y2]=[2y1002y2]. Evaluating at y0=Ax0=[1234][10]=[13], we get dzdy|y0=[2(1)002(3)]=[2006].

  • The function y acts on a vector x∈R2 by multiplying it by A and outputs a vector y(x)∈R2. Thus, dydx=A.

Therefore, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))|x0=dfdz|z0⋅dzdy|y0⋅dydx|x0=[5101]⋅[2006]⋅[1234]=[10606]⋅[1234]=[28441824].

For x,y,z∈R2, consider the following functions:

y(x)=AxwhereA=[1234]z(y)=[y12y22]f(z)=CzwhereC=[5101] What is ddxf(z(y(x))) evaluated at x0=[10]?

Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Using the chain rule, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))=dfdz⋅dzdy⋅dydx.

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

  • The function f acts on a vector z∈R2 by multiplying it by C and outputs a vector f(z)∈R2. Thus, dfdz=C.

  • The function z acts on a vector y∈R2 and outputs a vector z(y)∈R2. Thus, dzdy=[∂z1∂y1∂z1∂y2∂z2∂y1∂z2∂y2]=[2y1002y2]. Evaluating at y0=Ax0=[1234][10]=[13], we get dzdy|y0=[2(1)002(3)]=[2006].

  • The function y acts on a vector x∈R2 by multiplying it by A and outputs a vector y(x)∈R2. Thus, dydx=A.

Therefore, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))|x0=dfdz|z0⋅dzdy|y0⋅dydx|x0=[5101]⋅[2006]⋅[1234]=[10606]⋅[1234]=[28441824].

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Consider the functions $y:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2}$ and $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined by $$ y(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,f(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}]. $$ What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]?$
${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))|}_{{x}_{0}}=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} {{field-3}}
$38$ {{field-4}} $34$
question.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $f(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus, the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{y}_{1}}({y}_{1}-{y}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{y}_{2}}({y}_{1}-{y}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{y}_{1}}({y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{y}_{2}}({y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2{y}_{1} & 2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=y({x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}3\cdot 2+1 \\ 3+2\cdot 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 5\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 14 & 10\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{3}$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus, the total derivative of $y$ with respect to $x$ is a $2\times 3$ matrix

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{y}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{y}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{y}_{1}}{∂{x}_{3}} \\ \frac{∂{y}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{y}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{y}_{2}}{∂{x}_{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}{x}_{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & {x}_{1} & 1 \\ 1 & {x}_{3} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(y(x)){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 14 & 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 38 & 52 & 34\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Using the chain rule, we have

ddxf(y(x))=dfdy⋅dydx.

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

  • The function f acts on a vector y∈R2 and outputs a vector f(y)∈R2. Thus, the total derivative of f with respect to y is a 2×2 matrix dfdy=[∂f1∂y1∂f1∂y2∂f2∂y1∂f2∂y2]=[∂∂y1(y1−y2)∂∂y2(y1−y2)∂∂y1(y12+y22)∂∂y2(y12+y22)]=[1−12y12y2]. Evaluating at y0=y(x0)=[3⋅2+13+2⋅1]=[75], we get dfdy|y0=[1−11410].
  • The function y acts on a vector x∈R3 and outputs a vector y(x)∈R2. Thus, the total derivative of y with respect to x is a 2×3 matrix dydx=[∂y1∂x1∂y1∂x2∂y1∂x3∂y2∂x1∂y2∂x2∂y2∂x3]=[∂∂x1(x1x2+x3)∂∂x2(x1x2+x3)∂∂x3(x1x2+x3)∂∂x1(x1+x2x3)∂∂x2(x1+x2x3)∂∂x3(x1+x2x3)]=[x2x111x3x2]. Evaluating at x0=[321], we get dydx|x0=[231112].

Therefore, we have ddxf(y(x))|x0=dfdy|y0⋅dydx|x0=[1−11410]⋅[231112]=[12−1385234].

question.problem:
For $x,y,z\in {R}^{2},$ consider the following functions: 

$$
\begin{aligned} & y(x)=Ax\,\text{where}\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & z(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & f(z)=Cz\,\text{where}\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & {y}_{1} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$

Question 4
?

For x,y,z∈R2, consider the following functions:

y(x)=AxwhereA=[1−120]z(y)=[y1y2y1+y2]f(z)=CzwhereC=[4215] What is ddxf(z(y(x))) evaluated at x0=[01]?

a
[−5312]
b
[13−24]
c
[4−20−5]
d
[−2−213−5]
e
[2−2−135]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the chain rule, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))=dfdz⋅dzdy⋅dydx.

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

  • The function f acts on a vector z∈R2 by multiplying it by C and outputs a vector f(z)∈R2. Thus, dfdz=C.

  • The function z acts on a vector y∈R2 and outputs a vector z(y)∈R2. Thus, dzdy=[∂z1∂y1∂z1∂y2∂z2∂y1∂z2∂y2]=[y2y111]. Evaluating at y0=Ax0=[1−120][01]=[−10], we get dzdy|y0=[0−111].

  • The function y acts on a vector x∈R2 by multiplying it by A and outputs a vector y(x)∈R2. Thus, dydx=A.

Therefore, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))|x0=dfdz|z0⋅dzdy|y0⋅dydx|x0=[4215]⋅[0−111]⋅[1−120]=[2−254]⋅[1−120]=[−2−213−5].

last_observation.name: Question 4
last_observation.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & {y}_{1} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=A{x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x))){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}{|}_{{z}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 13 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 4
question.problem:
For $x,y,z\in {R}^{2},$ consider the following functions: 

$$
\begin{aligned} & y(x)=Ax\,\text{where}\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & z(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & f(z)=Cz\,\text{where}\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & {y}_{1} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=A{x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x))){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}{|}_{{z}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 13 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

For x,y,z∈R2, consider the following functions:

y(x)=AxwhereA=[1−120]z(y)=[y1y2y1+y2]f(z)=CzwhereC=[4215] What is ddxf(z(y(x))) evaluated at x0=[01]?

a
[−5312]
b
[13−24]
c
[4−20−5]
d
[−2−213−5]
e
[2−2−135]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Using the chain rule, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))=dfdz⋅dzdy⋅dydx.

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

  • The function f acts on a vector z∈R2 by multiplying it by C and outputs a vector f(z)∈R2. Thus, dfdz=C.

  • The function z acts on a vector y∈R2 and outputs a vector z(y)∈R2. Thus, dzdy=[∂z1∂y1∂z1∂y2∂z2∂y1∂z2∂y2]=[y2y111]. Evaluating at y0=Ax0=[1−120][01]=[−10], we get dzdy|y0=[0−111].

  • The function y acts on a vector x∈R2 by multiplying it by A and outputs a vector y(x)∈R2. Thus, dydx=A.

Therefore, we have

ddxf(z(y(x)))|x0=dfdz|z0⋅dzdy|y0⋅dydx|x0=[4215]⋅[0−111]⋅[1−120]=[2−254]⋅[1−120]=[−2−213−5].

solution.reasoning: At x_0=(0,1), y(x_0)=(-1,0). Thus Dz=[[0,-1],[1,1]]. By the chain rule, D(f∘z∘y)(x_0)=C Dz A=[[4,2],[1,5]][[-2,0],[3,-1]]=[[-2,-2],[13,-5]], matching option d. No captured MA answer or grade establishes its stated key.

feedback.problem:
For $x,y,z\in {R}^{2},$ consider the following functions: 

$$
\begin{aligned} & y(x)=Ax\,\text{where}\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & z(y)=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}{y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & f(z)=Cz\,\text{where}\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

What is $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))$ evaluated at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the chain rule, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x)))=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let's consider each of the factors in turn.

- The function $f$ acts on a vector $z\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $C$ and outputs a vector $f(z)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}=C.
$$

- The function $z$ acts on a vector $y\in {R}^{2}$ and outputs a vector $z(y)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{1}}{∂{y}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{1}} & \frac{∂{z}_{2}}{∂{y}_{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{2} & {y}_{1} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating at ${y}_{0}=A{x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- The function $y$ acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{2}$ by multiplying it by $A$ and outputs a vector $y(x)\in {R}^{2}.$ Thus,

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=A.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}f(z(y(x))){|}_{{x}_{0}} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}z}{|}_{{z}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}y}{|}_{{y}_{0}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ 13 & -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 1
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 2
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=y-x$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-3\le y\le 0.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 3
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=2x-4y$ for $-2\le x\le 0$ and $-1\le y\le 5.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2u-4v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-4v} \\  & =⟨2u-4v+u,\,v+2(2u-4v),\,u-4v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-4v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-7v)\cdot 4+(u-4v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6u+8v+16u-28v+u-4v \\  & =11u-24v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$

$$

questions.name: Question 4
questions.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x-3y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.name: Question 5
questions.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}-Q\frac{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}{∂y}+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}})\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
questions.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula
questions.raw_html:
5.Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral Using a Formula?

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(−P∂gA−QA∂y+A)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

E
Wed, Oct 14th @ 10:09 PM|Elapsed: 0:15Correct

observed_steps.name: Question 1
observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?

EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u+v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):0≤u≤4,−2≤v≤3}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(u+v)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(u+v)⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk101011|=⟨|0111|,−|1101|,|1001|⟩=⟨−1,−1,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩|x=u,y=v,z=u+v=⟨u+v−v,2v−(u+v),uv⟩=⟨u,v−u,uv⟩

observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

over the domain

observed_steps.worked_solution:

$$

$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

$$

$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-4v} \\  & =⟨2u-4v+u,\,v+2(2u-4v),\,u-4v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-4v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-7v)\cdot 4+(u-4v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6u+8v+16u-28v+u-4v \\  & =11u-24v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 3
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨z+x,y+2z,x−4y⟩ and the surface S defined by z=2x−4y for −2≤x≤0 and −1≤y≤5. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as ∬SF⋅dS=∫−20∫−15AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
11u+4v
b
24uv
c
7uv−4v
d
u−v
e
11u−24v
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,2u−4v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):−2≤u≤0,−1≤v≤5}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(2u−4v)⟩=⟨1,0,2⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(2u−4v)⟩=⟨0,1,−4⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10201−4|=⟨|021−4|,−|120−4|,|1001|⟩=⟨−2,4,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z+x,y+2z,x−4y⟩|x=u,y=v,z=2u−4v=⟨2u−4v+u,v+2(2u−4v),u−4v⟩=⟨3u−4v,4u−7v,u−4v⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨3u−4v,4u−7v,u−4v⟩⋅⟨−2,4,1⟩=(3u−4v)⋅(−2)+(4u−7v)⋅4+(u−4v)⋅1=−6u+8v+16u−28v+u−4v=11u−24v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z+x,y+2z,x−4y⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(11u−24v)dA=∫−20∫−15(11u−24v)dvdu.

observed_steps.name: Question 4
observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 4
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x-3y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?

$$

over the domain 

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}

$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}

Question 4
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,2z,y+z⟩ and the surface S defined by z=x−3y for −1≤x≤2 and −1≤y≤3. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as
∬SF⋅dS=∫−12∫−13AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
12u−v
b
8u+14v
c
u−6v
d
5u−17v
e
8u−23v
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u−3v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):−1≤u≤2,−1≤v≤3}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(u−3v)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(u−3v)⟩=⟨0,1,−3⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10101−3|=⟨|011−3|,−|110−3|,|1001|⟩=⟨−1,3,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨x+z,2z,y+z⟩|x=u,y=v,z=u−3v=⟨u+u−3v,2(u−3v),v+u−3v⟩=⟨2u−3v,2u−6v,u−2v⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨2u−3v,2u−6v,u−2v⟩⋅⟨−1,3,1⟩=(2u−3v)⋅(−1)+(2u−6v)⋅(3)+(u−2v)⋅1=−2u+3v+6u−18v+u−2v=5u−17v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(5u−17v)dA=∫−12∫−13(5u−17v)dvdu.

observed_steps.name: Question 5
observed_steps.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}-Q\frac{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}{∂y}+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}})\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(−P∂gA−QA∂y+A)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
∂x,∂g, and −R
b
∂x,∂g, and R
c
∂z,∂g, and −1
d
∂x,∂g, and −1
e
 ∂x,∂g, and 1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form z=g(x,y), it can be parameterized as

r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,0,∂g∂x⟩ry′=⟨0,1,∂g∂y⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×ry′=|ijk10∂g∂x01∂g∂y|=⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(rx′×ry′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩dA=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

judgments.reasoning: The induced normal is r_u×r_v=⟨-1,-1,1⟩, and F(r)=⟨u,v-u,uv⟩. Their dot product is -u-(v-u)+uv=uv-v, confirming my earlier answer, option e. MA's worked solution agrees. The submitted option a, uv+v, differs from this expression and was correctly graded Incorrect.

For r(u,v)=⟨u,v,v-u⟩, r_u×r_v=⟨1,-1,1⟩. The integrand is (u+v)^2-(u-v)^2+uv=5uv, option d. This confirms my earlier answer and agrees with both the submitted value graded Correct and MA's worked solution.

The parametrization gives r_u×r_v=⟨-2,4,1⟩ and F(r)=⟨3u-4v,4u-7v,u-4v⟩. Their dot product is -2(3u-4v)+4(4u-7v)+(u-4v)=11u-24v, confirming my earlier answer, option e. MA's worked solution agrees. The actual submitted option a, 11u+4v, was correctly graded Incorrect.

My earlier answer, option d, is correct: r_u×r_v=⟨-1,3,1⟩ gives -(2u-3v)+3(2u-6v)+(u-2v)=5u-17v. MA's answer and Correct grade agree. However, the worked solution's final display mistakenly replaces the given field with ⟨z-y,2y-z,xy⟩. That field would produce uv-4u+19v on this surface, so the final displayed equality contains a source error despite the correct answer and preceding derivation.

The upward vector area element is ⟨-g_x,-g_y,1⟩ dA, so its dot product with ⟨P,Q,R⟩ is -P∂g/∂x-Q∂g/∂y+R. The missing parts are ∂x, ∂g, and R, option b. My earlier answer agrees with MA's worked solution and the submitted response graded Correct.

question.name: Question 1
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩ and the surface S defined by z=x+y for 0≤x≤4 and −2≤y≤3. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as ∬SF⋅dS=∫04∫−23AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
uv+v
b
u2+uv+v2
c
u+v
d
2u2v−uv+v2
e
uv−v
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u+v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):0≤u≤4,−2≤v≤3}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(u+v)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(u+v)⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk101011|=⟨|0111|,−|1101|,|1001|⟩=⟨−1,−1,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩|x=u,y=v,z=u+v=⟨u+v−v,2v−(u+v),uv⟩=⟨u,v−u,uv⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨u,v−u,uv⟩⋅⟨−1,−1,1⟩=u⋅(−1)+(v−u)⋅(−1)+uv⋅1=−u−v+u+uv=uv−v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(uv−v)dA=∫04∫−23uv−vdvdu.

last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩ and the surface S defined by z=x+y for 0≤x≤4 and −2≤y≤3. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as ∬SF⋅dS=∫04∫−23AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
uv+v
b
u2+uv+v2
c
u+v
d
2u2v−uv+v2
e
uv−v
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u+v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):0≤u≤4,−2≤v≤3}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(u+v)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(u+v)⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk101011|=⟨|0111|,−|1101|,|1001|⟩=⟨−1,−1,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩|x=u,y=v,z=u+v=⟨u+v−v,2v−(u+v),uv⟩=⟨u,v−u,uv⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨u,v−u,uv⟩⋅⟨−1,−1,1⟩=u⋅(−1)+(v−u)⋅(−1)+uv⋅1=−u−v+u+uv=uv−v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(uv−v)dA=∫04∫−23uv−vdvdu.

solution.reasoning: With r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u+v⟩, r_u×r_v=⟨-1,-1,1⟩ and F(r(u,v))=⟨u,v-u,uv⟩. Their dot product is -u-(v-u)+uv=uv-v, giving option e for the orientation induced by the parametrization. The opposite orientation reverses the sign; the problem does not explicitly specify orientation. No captured MA answer evidence is supplied.

feedback.name: Question 1
feedback.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x+y$ for $0\le x\le 4$ and $-2\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u+v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 4,\,-2\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u+v} \\  & =⟨u+v-v,\,2v-(u+v),\,uv⟩ \\  & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨u,\,v-u,\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =u\cdot (-1)+(v-u)\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =-u-v+u+uv \\  & =uv-v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(uv-v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{-2}^{3}uv-v\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

question.name: Question 2
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=y-x$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $-3\le y\le 0.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨(x+y)2,(x−y)2,xy⟩ and the surface S defined by z=y−x for −1≤x≤1 and −3≤y≤0. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as ∬SF⋅dS=∫−11∫−30AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
3uv2
b
uv+v
c
uv−v
d
5uv
e
−uv
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,v−u⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):−1≤u≤1,−3≤v≤0}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(v−u)⟩=⟨1,0,−1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(v−u)⟩=⟨0,1,1⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10−1011|=⟨|0−111|,−|1−101|,|1001|⟩=⟨1,−1,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨(x+y)2,(x−y)2,xy⟩|x=u,y=v,z=v−u=⟨(u+v)2,(u−v)2,uv⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨(u+v)2,(u−v)2,uv⟩⋅⟨1,−1,1⟩=(u+v)2⋅1+(u−v)2⋅(−1)+uv⋅1=5uv.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨(x+y)2,(x−y)2,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(5uv)dA=∫−11∫−305uvdvdu.

last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,v-u⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 1,\,-3\le v\le 0\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v-u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=v-u} \\  & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨(u+v)^{2},\,(u-v)^{2},\,uv⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-1,\,1⟩ \\  & =(u+v)^{2}\cdot 1+(u-v)^{2}\cdot (-1)+uv\cdot 1 \\  & =5uv.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨(x+y)^{2},\,(x-y)^{2},\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5uv)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-3}^{0}5uv\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}

question.name: Question 3
question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=2x-4y$ for $-2\le x\le 0$ and $-1\le y\le 5.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2u-4v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-4v} \\  & =⟨2u-4v+u,\,v+2(2u-4v),\,u-4v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-4v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-7v)\cdot 4+(u-4v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6u+8v+16u-28v+u-4v \\  & =11u-24v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,2u-4v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-2\le u\le 0,\,-1\le v\le 5\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u-4v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=2u-4v} \\  & =⟨2u-4v+u,\,v+2(2u-4v),\,u-4v⟩ \\  & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨3u-4v,\,4u-7v,\,u-4v⟩\cdot ⟨-2,\,4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(3u-4v)\cdot (-2)+(4u-7v)\cdot 4+(u-4v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-6u+8v+16u-28v+u-4v \\  & =11u-24v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z+x,\,y+2z,\,x-4y⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-1}^{5}(11u-24v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=x-3y$ for $-1\le x\le 2$ and $-1\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

last_observation.name: Question 4
last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,u-3v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-1\le u\le 2,\,-1\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u-3v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨x+z,\,2z,\,y+z⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=u-3v} \\  & =⟨u+u-3v,\,2(u-3v),\,v+u-3v⟩ \\  & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨2u-3v,\,2u-6v,\,u-2v⟩\cdot ⟨-1,\,3,\,1⟩ \\  & =(2u-3v)\cdot (-1)+(2u-6v)\cdot (3)+(u-2v)\cdot 1 \\  & =-2u+3v+6u-18v+u-2v \\  & =5u-17v.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨z-y,\,2y-z,\,xy⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{3}(5u-17v)\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,2z,y+z⟩ and the surface S defined by z=x−3y for −1≤x≤2 and −1≤y≤3. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as
∬SF⋅dS=∫−12∫−13AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
12u−v
b
8u+14v
c
u−6v
d
5u−17v
e
8u−23v
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u−3v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):−1≤u≤2,−1≤v≤3}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(u−3v)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(u−3v)⟩=⟨0,1,−3⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10101−3|=⟨|011−3|,−|110−3|,|1001|⟩=⟨−1,3,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨x+z,2z,y+z⟩|x=u,y=v,z=u−3v=⟨u+u−3v,2(u−3v),v+u−3v⟩=⟨2u−3v,2u−6v,u−2v⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨2u−3v,2u−6v,u−2v⟩⋅⟨−1,3,1⟩=(2u−3v)⋅(−1)+(2u−6v)⋅(3)+(u−2v)⋅1=−2u+3v+6u−18v+u−2v=5u−17v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(5u−17v)dA=∫−12∫−13(5u−17v)dvdu.

Question 4
?

Consider the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨x+z,2z,y+z⟩ and the surface S defined by z=x−3y for −1≤x≤2 and −1≤y≤3. Using the parametrization x=u and y=v, the flux of F through S can be expressed as
∬SF⋅dS=∫−12∫−13AAAAAAAdvdu. What is the missing expression?

a
12u−v
b
8u+14v
c
u−6v
d
5u−17v
e
8u−23v
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Using the parametrization, where x=u and y=v, our surface can be parameterized as

r(u,v)=⟨u,v,u−3v⟩

over the domain

D={(u,v):−1≤u≤2,−1≤v≤3}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u),∂∂u(v),∂∂u(u−3v)⟩=⟨1,0,1⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u),∂∂v(v),∂∂v(u−3v)⟩=⟨0,1,−3⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk10101−3|=⟨|011−3|,−|110−3|,|1001|⟩=⟨−1,3,1⟩.

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of r(u,v) into F(x,y,z):

F(r(u,v))=⟨x+z,2z,y+z⟩|x=u,y=v,z=u−3v=⟨u+u−3v,2(u−3v),v+u−3v⟩=⟨2u−3v,2u−6v,u−2v⟩

Then, we calculate the dot product of F and ru′×rv′:

F(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)=⟨2u−3v,2u−6v,u−2v⟩⋅⟨−1,3,1⟩=(2u−3v)⋅(−1)+(2u−6v)⋅(3)+(u−2v)⋅1=−2u+3v+6u−18v+u−2v=5u−17v.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬S⟨z−y,2y−z,xy⟩⋅dS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA=∬D(5u−17v)dA=∫−12∫−13(5u−17v)dvdu.

question.name: Question 5
question.problem:
For a surface $S$ given by $z=g(x,y)$ for $(x,y)\in D,$ the flux of the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}-Q\frac{\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}}}{∂y}+\bbox[3pt,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{A}})\,\text{d}A.
$$

From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(−P∂gA−QA∂y+A)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
∂x,∂g, and −R
b
∂x,∂g, and R
c
∂z,∂g, and −1
d
∂x,∂g, and −1
e
 ∂x,∂g, and 1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form z=g(x,y), it can be parameterized as

r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,0,∂g∂x⟩ry′=⟨0,1,∂g∂y⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×ry′=|ijk10∂g∂x01∂g∂y|=⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(rx′×ry′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩dA=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

last_observation.name: Question 5
last_observation.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Since our surface $S$ is of the form $z=g(x,y),$ it can be parameterized as

$$
r(x,y)=⟨x,\,y,\,g(x,y)⟩.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨1,\,0,\,\frac{∂g}{∂x}⟩ \\ {r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨0,\,1,\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & \frac{∂g}{∂x} \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{∂g}{∂y}\end{aligned}|=⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(x,y))\cdot ({r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{y}^{′})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{∂g}{∂x},\,-\frac{∂g}{∂y},\,1⟩\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

question.html:
Question 5
?

For a surface S given by z=g(x,y) for (x,y)∈D, the flux of the vector field F(x,y,z)=⟨P,Q,R⟩ over S is given by ∬SF⋅dS=∬D(−P∂gA−QA∂y+A)dA. From left to right, what are the missing parts of the formula?

a
∂x,∂g, and −R
b
∂x,∂g, and R
c
∂z,∂g, and −1
d
∂x,∂g, and −1
e
 ∂x,∂g, and 1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface S with parametrization r(u,v) for (u,v)∈D, the flux of a vector field F over S is given by

∬SF⋅dS=∬SF⋅ndS=∬DF(r(u,v))⋅(ru′×rv′)dA.

Since our surface S is of the form z=g(x,y), it can be parameterized as

r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨1,0,∂g∂x⟩ry′=⟨0,1,∂g∂y⟩

Now, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×ry′=|ijk10∂g∂x01∂g∂y|=⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩.

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

∬SF⋅dS=∬DF(r(x,y))⋅(rx′×ry′)dA=∬D⟨P,Q,R⟩⋅⟨−∂g∂x,−∂g∂y,1⟩dA=∬D(−P∂g∂x−Q∂g∂y+R)dA.

solution.reasoning: For the upward orientation, r(x,y)=⟨x,y,g(x,y)⟩ gives r_x×r_y=⟨-g_x,-g_y,1⟩. Dotting with ⟨P,Q,R⟩ yields -P∂g/∂x-Q∂g/∂y+R. The missing parts are ∂x, ∂g, and R, option b. No captured MA answer evidence establishes its key.
